written_by: Mark · Live Pulse 06:30 (from the Morning Pulse)
headline: Asia buys back the chip sell-off without a New York lead, while fresh US tariffs and Sunday's OPEC+ clash are the risks not yet in prices

findings.headline: The Bank of Korea hiked and Seoul rallied anyway: the move was priced
findings.body: Korea's central bank raised rates at its last decision of the year, citing the AI chip boom, and the market treated it as expected rather than as a brake. With US cash shut for Thanksgiving, Taiwan and Korea are being driven by the same memory and foundry names that sank on Wednesday, so this is one sector swinging both indices, not a broad vote of confidence. Thin holiday liquidity makes a fade at the European open the main risk.

FT: Stocks advance in Asia after volatile US trading over AI risks

findings.headline: Washington announced new tariffs on a host of countries, China included
findings.body: The tariff announcement landed overnight while US cash markets were closed, so Wall Street has not had a session to price it and Asia is trading through it on a chip bounce. It adds trade risk to a backdrop where firmer core PCE inflation already keeps the Fed leaning towards tightening. Watch how Europe's exporters and China-exposed names open at 09:00.

FT: US PCE inflation keeps Fed on course for more tightening

findings.headline: OPEC+'s largest members head into Sunday's meeting at odds over production estimates
findings.body: Analysts expect the 29 November ministerial meeting to be one of the most complicated in years, with the biggest producers disagreeing over production estimates. Crude is carrying that uncertainty plus a lingering Gulf risk premium, and funds are lightly positioned, so a surprise either way can move prices fast. The outcome lands after Friday's short US session, leaving Monday's open to absorb it.

sources.label: FT: Opec+'s largest members head for clash over oil production estimates

view: Our view: Asia's bounce is a chip trade on thin holiday volume, not a verdict that Tuesday's AI doubts are over; the overnight tariffs and the OPEC+ dispute are the two developments prices have not fully reacted to. The ECB's October account at 13:30 Zurich is Europe's only scheduled catalyst today.
